stances.claim: After two acquittals and the third-case bail denial, De Lima has four possible routes to freedom - MR on the bail denial; certiorari to CA or SC alleging grave abuse; habeas corpus to the SC under the Reyes v. Director exception; and relentless pursuit of trial on the merits for an acquittal.

Route 1 (MR) argues Buenaventura erred by using prima facie/probable cause standards instead of the constitutional 'strong evidence of guilt'; relying absolutely on direct examination of 'convict-witnesses' without regard to cross-examination; failing to discuss their inherent unreliability as moral-turpitude convicts; and refusing to believe Benjamin Magalong, the only credible prosecution witness, who testified De Lima was merely performing her SoJ duties in purging the NBP of drug trading.

The MR also alleges grave abuse of discretion in ignoring legal sanctions against criminal-convict witnesses; admitting hearsay; belittling humanitarian issues (hypertension, diabetes, cervical spondylosis with chronic neck pain and severe headaches); dismissing the October 9, 2022 hostage incident as 'isolated'; and disbelieving she is not a flight risk given her stature, public record, integrity, advanced age, frail health, and political-persecution context.
Route 2 (certiorari): If the MR is denied, the grave-abuse claims can be the bases of a petition in the CA or SC - and an MR is legally a prerequisite before certiorari can prosper.

Route 3 (habeas corpus to SC): Possible if De Lima's lawyers can demonstrate facts on all fours with Reyes v. Director - where Gigi Reyes was freed via Estelito Mendoza's showing of 'vexatious, capricious, and oppressive' custody. CJ already urged this in his January 30 column 'Gigi freed, Leila next?' - but De Lima's lawyers preferred the conventional bail route over the speedy unconventional habeas corpus remedy.

stances.claim: Route 4 (relentless trial pursuit): If De Lima's counsels secured acquittals in two prior cases, they should be able to do it again - with the trial judge's prerogative after due process to limit the 20 additional prosecution witnesses. Buenaventura's inhibition means the new presiding magistrate may need more than nine months.

Of these four routes, the most important is the fourth - because victory in Route 4 entitles De Lima to permanent and complete freedom via acquittal, while victories in Routes 1, 2, and 3 entitle her merely to temporary liberty pending trial. The great challenge to her lawyers is to secure her acquittal 'because of her innocence, not merely because of reasonable doubt on her guilt.'

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban tracks four possible routes by which former Senator Leila de Lima might continue her quest for freedom after the third Muntinlupa RTC's bail denial - having been acquitted in two of the three 2017 illegal-drug-trading cases (the prosecutors' MR on the second acquittal discussed June 5 / A107) and now seeking review of the third (discussed June 12 / A106). Court administrator Raul B. Villanueva had directed Judge Romeo S. Buenaventura to finish the case in nine months, and Buenaventura accordingly rushed the schedule before his inhibition last Friday. Route 1 is De Lima's MR on the bail denial, which argues Buenaventura used wrong legal standards (prima facie / probable cause instead of the constitutional 'strong evidence of guilt'), relied 'absolutely and completely' on direct examination of 'convict-witnesses' without regard to cross-examination, failed to discuss their inherent unreliability as moral-turpitude convicts, and refused to believe Benjamin Magalong (the only credible prosecution witness, who testified De Lima was merely performing her SoJ duties in purging the NBP of drug trading) - and alleges grave abuse of discretion in admitting hearsay, belittling humanitarian issues (hypertension, diabetes, cervical spondylosis with chronic neck pain and severe headaches), dismissing the October 9, 2022 hostage incident as 'isolated' despite it almost killing her, and disbelieving she is not a flight risk given her stature, public record, integrity, advanced age, frail health, and political-persecution context. Route 2 is certiorari to the CA or SC alleging grave abuse - with the MR being a prerequisite. Route 3 is a direct petition for habeas corpus to the SC under the Reyes v. Director (January 17, 2023) exception, where Gigi Reyes was freed via Estelito P. Mendoza's showing that her custody had become 'vexatious, capricious, and oppressive amounting to an infringement of the constitutional right to speedy trial' - a route Panganiban had urged in his January 30 column 'Gigi freed, Leila next?,' but De Lima's lawyers preferred the conventional bail-petition route over the speedy unconventional habeas corpus remedy. Route 4 is relentless pursuit of trial on the merits to secure permanent freedom via acquittal; with two prior acquittals already secured, De Lima's counsels should be able to do it again, though the new presiding magistrate after Buenaventura's inhibition may need more than nine months to study the case, conduct trials, and rule on whether to limit the prosecution's announced 20 additional witnesses. Of the four routes, Panganiban ranks Route 4 most important - because victory there entitles De Lima to permanent and complete freedom via acquittal, while victories in the first three give her merely temporary liberty pending trial. The great challenge to her lawyers is to secure her acquittal 'because of her innocence, not merely because of reasonable doubt on her guilt.'
